title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: Held because the catalog is labelled user-opt-in without evidence establishing its default on arrival. Microsoft documents a maker-selected Browse skills preview, but the briefing correctly acknowledges that its relationship to the planned catalog is unconfirmed. The roadmap facts and package-management calls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Copilot Studio skills catalog in which makers can discover organisational skills.
claims.quote: With the Skills catalog in Copilot Studio, makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the Copilot Studio catalog by the roadmap's name.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog; skills catalog Copilot Studio Microsoft 365 App Store. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview and plugins/administrator-guide; results document Browse skills preview and other products' catalogs, not the named Studio catalog.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented preview lets a maker open an agent, select Build, the plus icon beside Skills, Browse skills (preview), a shared skill, and Add.
claims.quote: Select the Build tab. Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). Browse the shared skills available to you. Select the skill you want to add. On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.claim: Browse skills lists skills shared with the maker by admins or skill owners.
claims.quote: You can browse and add skills that other people shared with you to your agent. The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An instruction-based skill is defined by a name, description and instructions guiding the agent for specific tasks.
claims.quote: A skill is a capability defined by a name, a description, and instructions that tell the agent how to handle specific types of tasks or scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An agent gets a snapshot when a maker adds a shared skill.
claims.quote: When you add a shared skill, the agent gets a snapshot of the skill while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The added snapshot retains a reference to the original shared skill.
claims.quote: the agent gets a snapshot of the skill while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A maker receives an update notification when opening an agent using an older shared-skill version.
claims.quote: You receive a skill update notification when you open an agent that uses an older version of a shared skill.

claims.claim: The maker can choose to update the shared skill to the new version.
claims.quote: You can choose to update to the new version by selecting the update button for the skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: A maker sharing a skill they created can choose Only you or Specific users or groups in your organization.
claims.quote: Only you: Keeps the skill private to your account. Specific users or groups in your organization: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address. People and groups you add can use the skill.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The people and groups a maker shares a skill with can add it to their agents.
claims.quote: The people and groups you share with can then add the skill to their agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An owner must reshare an edited shared skill to make its latest version available to existing recipients.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.claim: A skill package can contain supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The orchestration runtime selects a skill from the user's request and the skill description rather than requiring a request naming the skill.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description. When the runtime activates a skill, the skill's instructions guide your agent's behavior for that specific task.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct the agent to use a particular tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.claim: The Learn shared-skill page does not specify the planned catalog skill's data-access boundaries.
claims.quote: Searched: Browse skills approval data catalog; Copilot Studio skills catalog. Opened skills-manage and skills-overview. They describe shared snapshots and instructions, not data-access boundaries for the roadmap's catalog.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an additional approval step after selecting Add for a shared skill in Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Browse skills approval data catalog; Copilot Studio skills catalog roles approval. Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. The Browse skills procedure ends with Add; package and MCP approvals are separate procedures.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level switch for the Copilot Studio maker skill-sharing control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Browse skills admin disable sharing permissions default catalog; Browse skills sharing tenant switch. Opened skills-manage, faqs-copilot-harness and business-skill-overview. Agent sharing, Work IQ business skills and package controls do not establish this switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned Copilot Studio skills catalog has a user-opt-in default on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: skills catalog Copilot Studio default; Copilot Studio Browse skills admin disable sharing permissions default catalog. Opened skills-manage and faqs-copilot-harness; neither establishes the roadmap catalog's default or identifies it as the documented Browse skills preview.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "unknown". Keep "Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival" in Why it matters: the maker-selected Browse skills preview does not establish the planned catalog's default while their equivalence remains unconfirmed.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified a required administrator rollout action for the planned catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog roles approval; skills catalog Copilot Studio Microsoft 365 App Store; Browse skills admin disable sharing. Read the roadmap, skills-manage and package governance pages; none maps the planned catalog to Browse skills or specifies its rollout action.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption licensing and variable cost reflect documented Copilot Credit billing for agents on the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The shared-skills page warns that using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts when a maker starts building.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog license price roles approval; Copilot Studio skills catalog price licensing. Opened skills-manage and billing-credit-overview; read billing-licensing search excerpts. General product entitlement and harness consumption are stated, not a catalog-specific licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate charge or rate for browsing, adding or sharing a catalog skill.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog price licensing; Browse skills harness license. Opened skills-manage, skills-add-existing and billing-credit-overview; read billing-rate search excerpts. No separate browse, add or share rate was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog price licensing; Browse skills harness license. Opened billing-credit-overview and skills-manage; read requirements-messages-management search excerpt. Found general harness billing, not a catalog-specific credit rate.

claims.claim: An agent using shared skills remains subject to its harness's documented billing.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The cited plugins-management page names AI Administrator and Global Administrator for MCP registration review and tenant-wide consent, not skill management.
claims.quote: You must have access to the Tools page ... to manage agent tools and review MCP server registration requests. You must be able to grant tenant-wide consent. Two roles meet both requirements: AI Administrator. Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users reaches package user availability.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. Select the plugin that you want to manage. Open Users, and then choose ... All users ... No users ... Specific users and groups
claims.fix: Complete the path as "Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users > All users / No users / Specific users and groups". The cited page documents these availability choices; the printed path currently stops on their containing tab.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} changes availability through availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}; allowedUsersAndGroups: Users/groups for whom the package is available. availableTo: Enum value specifying which users or groups within the tenant can access this package. Required if updating allowedUsersAndGroups.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block blocks the selected skill package.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block prevents package usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
